headline: DigiCert breach exposes customer identity documents; Zyxel GS1900 patch fails against zero-day; WordPress KEV patch due Nov 6

bullets.text: New: BleepingComputer reports a DigiCert data breach exposed customer information and identity documents.
New: DataBreaches.net reports a Royal Cornwall Hospitals Trust data breach in the UK exposed health details of 7,715 staff.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets: Help Net Security reports patched switches remained open to an in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441). SecurityWeek says the hacks were a zero-day; The Hacker News says the patch fails to block root command execution.

Due tomorrow, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.

Still active, CVE-2024-27834, 2 outlets: The Hacker News reports hackers are exploiting a patched Apple flaw to deliver info-stealing malware, citing CISA. CISA KEV added it 2026-11-04, with a federal due date of 2026-11-18.
Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: SecurityWeek reports malicious updates served in an OpsShield supply chain attack. BleepingComputer says the hijacked autoupdate deployed a backdoor and stole data.

actions: Treat Zyxel GS1900 switches as still exposed even after patching: restrict access, check for compromise, watch for a new fix.
Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 (KEV due 2026-11-06).
Patch Apple devices for CVE-2024-27834 (KEV due 2026-11-18) and keep iOS and Android current against APT29-linked exploits.
Check Rails advisories and patch apps that accept ImageMagick uploads. Check Debian and Ubuntu advisories for the APT flaw.
Patch Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-104935 (KEV due dates 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13) and check for compromise.
DigiCert, Chainalysis users: heed notices. DreamHost: change FTP passwords, end webmail sessions. mSecure: follow reset warnings. cPGuard: hunt the backdoor.
